proxyHosts.coversSqliXssLfi: Covers SQLi, XSS, LFI, RCE and hundreds of other attack patterns

proxyHosts.hostnameUpstreamsAreResolved: Hostname upstreams are resolved at config-apply time
proxyHosts.ifSetSendsA: If set, sends a 302 redirect instead of the status/body above
proxyHosts.inheritUsesTheGlobal: Inherit uses the global setting. Enabled/Disabled overrides per host.
proxyHosts.inspectAndBlockMalicious: Inspect and block malicious requests via Coraza / OWASP CRS
proxyHosts.internallyRewriteTheRequest: Internally rewrite the request URI before proxying. The client URL is unchanged; the upstream sees the target URI.
proxyHosts.issueCertificatesFromA: Issue certificates from a CA on the Certificates page.
proxyHosts.jsonArrayOfCaddy: JSON array of Caddy handlers, run before the reverse proxy.
proxyHosts.keepThisHostOff: Keep this host off the public :80/:443 listener entirely. Uncheck to publish it in both places.
proxyHosts.leaveEmptyToProtect: Leave empty to protect entire domain. Comma-separated paths to protect specific routes only.
proxyHosts.leaveEmptyToRequire: Leave empty to require an identity for the whole host. Comma-separated paths gate only those routes.
proxyHosts.markUpstreamsUnhealthyBased: Mark upstreams unhealthy based on response failures
proxyHosts.modsecuritySeclangSyntaxAppended: ModSecurity SecLang syntax. Appended after OWASP CRS if enabled.
proxyHosts.mtlsRequiresTlsOn: mTLS requires TLS on this host
proxyHosts.name: Name
proxyHosts.nameOfTheCookie: Name of the cookie for sticky sessions
proxyHosts.noCustomHeadersUse: No custom headers — use the + button to add one.
proxyHosts.noMtlsRolesYet: No mTLS roles yet. Create roles on the Certificates page.
proxyHosts.noRolesOrCertificates: No roles or certificates are selected.
proxyHosts.noTailscaleAuthKey: No Tailscale auth key is stored
proxyHosts.noUsersOrGroups: No users or groups are selected, so forward auth will reject every request.
proxyHosts.nodeToDialThe: Node to dial the upstreams through, for a backend that only exists on your tailnet. Upstream IP pinning and custom DNS resolvers do not apply — names are resolved by MagicDNS on the far side.
proxyHosts.onePerLineOr: One per line or comma-separated. Wildcards like *.example.com are supported.
proxyHosts.oneResolverPerLine: One resolver per line (e.g., 1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9). Used for dynamic upstream DNS resolution.
proxyHosts.onlyDevicesSignedIn: Only devices signed in to your tailnet may reach this host, and the caller is identified by their tailnet login. Tagged devices are refused, since they have no user behind them.
proxyHosts.pathsThatBypassAny: Paths that bypass any matching Path Block and reach the upstream. Allows are folded into every block's matcher: a block fires only for requests that match its pattern and do not match any allow. Example: allow /secret + block /* means only /secret reaches the upstream; everything else returns the block status. Allows do not affect Path Rewrites.
proxyHosts.pathsThatBypassThe: Paths that bypass the identity check while everything else stays gated. Ignored if Protected Paths is set.
proxyHosts.pathsToExcludeFrom: Paths to exclude from mTLS. These paths bypass client certificate enforcement while all other paths remain protected. Ignored if Protected Paths is set.
proxyHosts.perHostResolversOverride: Per-host resolvers override global DNS settings
proxyHosts.periodicallyProbeUpstreamsTo: Periodically probe upstreams to check health
proxyHosts.prependThisPrefixTo: Prepend this prefix to every request before proxying (e.g. /recipes → /recipes/original/path)
proxyHosts.recommendedKeepEnabledOnly: Recommended: keep enabled. Only disable if using IP-based outpost access or troubleshooting routing issues.
proxyHosts.rejectReturns413Partial: Reject returns 413; Partial inspects what fits and forwards the rest.
proxyHosts.requireClientsToPresent: Require clients to present a trusted certificate to connect
proxyHosts.requireUsersToAuthenticate: Require users to authenticate via Caddy Proxy Manager before accessing this host
proxyHosts.restrictSpecificPathsTo: Restrict specific paths to certain roles or certificates. Paths without rules allow any trusted cert/role above.
proxyHosts.returnAStaticResponse: Return a static response (no proxying) for matching paths. Supports Caddy path patterns like /dns-query or /admin/*.
proxyHosts.rulesListedHereAre: Rules listed here are disabled via SecRuleRemoveById
proxyHosts.savingWillBeRefused: Saving will be refused. The node cannot register without a key, and Caddy rejects a configuration whose listener will not come up — that would stop every proxy host from being updated, not just this one. Add a key in Settings → Tailscale first.
proxyHosts.secretKeyForHmac: Secret key for HMAC cookie signing
proxyHosts.serveACustomResponse: Serve a custom response body when a request errors (e.g. 502/503 when the upstream is down, or 404). Comma-separate status codes, or leave blank to match every error. The original status code is preserved.
proxyHosts.serveThisHostOn: Serve this host on your tailnet instead of, or as well as, the public internet
proxyHosts.setsXTailscaleUser: Sets X-Tailscale-User, -Login, -Name, -Tailnet and -Profile-Picture on the proxied request. Any such header sent by the client is stripped first.
proxyHosts.tailscaleIsSwitchedOff: Tailscale is switched off in Settings
proxyHosts.theRequestHeaderTo: The request header to hash for upstream selection
proxyHosts.theseBypassRoleChecks: These bypass role checks for this path
proxyHosts.thisHostWillNot: This host will not be served at all until Settings → Tailscale is enabled — it is dropped from the configuration rather than published publicly.
proxyHosts.thisWillRemoveThe: This will remove the configuration for:
proxyHosts.useForAllPaths: Use * for all paths, /admin/* for prefix match
proxyHosts.usefulForUpstreamServices: Useful for upstream services that require specific DNS resolution, such as internal DNS or service discovery. Common resolvers: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare), 194.242.2.2 (Mullvad), 9.9.9.9 (Quad9).
proxyHosts.whenEnabledHostnameUpstreams: When enabled, hostname upstreams are written to Caddy as concrete IP dials. If this handler has multiple different HTTPS upstream hostnames, HTTPS pinning is skipped for those HTTPS upstreams to avoid SNI mismatch.

settings.aSecretIsConfigured: A secret is configured. Its existing value cannot be viewed.
settings.absoluteRelativeAndCaddy: Absolute, relative, and Caddy placeholder-based targets are supported.
settings.accessLogsLiveIn: Access logs live in the caddy-logs Docker volume
settings.addAProviderTo: Add a provider to enable single sign-on.
settings.anAgentRecreatesRebuilds: An agent recreates, rebuilds and configures the Caddy container on its host. The controller has no Docker access of its own, and no address for any Caddy — everything reaches a proxy through its agent.
settings.anyFinalHttpStatus: Any final HTTP status from 200 through 599.
settings.appliedOnlyWhenNo: Applied only when no configured proxy host matches the request.
settings.appliedToTheMain: Applied to the main HTTP server
settings.askTheRegistryBelow: Ask the registry below, a few times a day, whether a newer release has been published. This is the only request this app makes to the internet on its own.
settings.authKeysAreNot: Auth keys are not being checked
settings.automaticallyLinkOauthAccounts: Automatically link OAuth accounts to existing users with the same email address.
settings.bothResolvesAaaaA: Both resolves AAAA + A with IPv6 preferred ordering.
settings.caddyWritesNoStatus: Caddy writes no status line or body — the native equivalent of a “444 / no response” policy.
settings.catchesARevokedExpired: Catches a revoked, expired or mistyped key here instead of at the next config apply. Needs a Tailscale API access token, because an auth key cannot authenticate to the API.
settings.checkTheAuthKey: Check the auth key against the Tailscale API before saving
settings.cidrsIpsOrThe: CIDRs, IPs, or the private_ranges shorthand — one per line. When CPM runs behind another proxy, Caddy resolves the real client IP from these. Leave empty to keep the current behaviour.
settings.claimHoldingTheUser: Claim holding the user's groups. Use dots for nested claims, e.g. resource_access.cpm.roles. Remember to request a matching scope above.
settings.configuredHostsAlwaysRun: Configured hosts always run before this catch-all
settings.countryLookupsForAnalytics: Country lookups for analytics, and the country matching that geo blocking is built on. With this off, geo block fields are not offered and no country is recorded against an event.
settings.createsCpmGroupsFrom: Creates CPM groups from the remaining prefixed claims (with the prefix stripped) for forward-auth access control. Groups you created yourself are never modified.
settings.currentlySetByAn: Currently set by an environment variable
settings.defaultDomainShownWhen: Default domain shown when creating new proxy hosts.
settings.defaultGeoblockTrustedProxies: Default geoblock trusted proxies from this list
settings.deriveCpmRolesAnd: Derive CPM roles and groups from the identity provider's group claim.
settings.enableItUnderSettings: Enable it under Settings → Caddy Build and rebuild Caddy before using it for DNS-01 challenges. Credentials saved now will not be used until then.
settings.ephemeralNodesDisappearFrom: Ephemeral nodes disappear from the tailnet when Caddy stops, instead of lingering as offline machines. Their identity is not reused, so a restart shows up as a new device.
settings.everyAgentRunsThe: Every agent runs the same configuration
settings.forHttpsTheResponse: For HTTPS the response can only be sent once a TLS certificate completes the handshake, so an unknown hostname or direct IP may fail earlier.
settings.forOidcProvidersThe: For OIDC providers, the issuer URL enables automatic discovery of endpoints.
settings.forUsersWithNo: For users with no icon of their own, look one up from gravatar.com by their email address. Their browser contacts gravatar.com directly, which discloses their IP and a hash of their address to a third party. Accounts with a local-only address are never looked up, and anyone without a Gravatar falls back to their initial.
settings.fromYourMaxmindAccount: From your MaxMind account. Without a subscription the databases cannot be downloaded, though GeoIP still works if you supply the files another way.
settings.gravatarIsSetBy: Gravatar is set by the AVATAR_GRAVATAR environment variable
settings.headersCaddyReadsThe: Headers Caddy reads the client IP from — one per line. Empty defaults to X-Forwarded-For. Set Cf-Connecting-Ip for Cloudflare, etc.
settings.hostAndPortE: Host and port, e.g. agent.example.com:3100. Defaults to port 3100.
settings.hostLevelSettingsCan: Host-level settings can override this default
settings.howLongEventsAre: How long events are kept. Lowering it migrates the existing tables' TTL, which rewrites their parts.
settings.ifTheAcmeEndpoint: If the ACME endpoint's TLS certificate is signed by an internal root not in the system trust store, paste the root (or chain) here so Caddy can connect to it.
settings.itIsReachedOver: It is reached over a socket on the shared data volume and needs no pairing. Pair a remote agent below only if Caddy runs on a different host from this controller.
settings.leaveEmptyToUse: Leave empty to use the Let's Encrypt default. For an internal CA (OpenBao, Step-CA, Windows ADCS), paste its ACME directory URL — must be HTTPS.
settings.leaveFieldsBlankTo: Leave fields blank to keep existing values.
settings.n307And308Preserve: 307 and 308 preserve the original request method.
settings.name: Name
settings.nameTheGroupsExactly: Name the groups exactly as your provider reports them. Separate several with commas — platform-owners, sre-oncall — and any one of them grants the role. A role left blank falls back to the prefix above, so the two styles can be mixed. The most privileged match wins.
settings.newPasswordsAreHashed: New passwords are hashed with argon2id. Accounts created before that change still use bcrypt, which caps the password at 72 bytes. Turning this on sends those users to a reset screen at their next sign-in; choosing a new password upgrades the hash and clears the prompt. Users who sign in through an OAuth/OIDC provider have no password and are never asked.
settings.noAgentIsAnswering: No agent is answering, so the container cannot be managed from here
settings.nothingElseOnThe: Nothing else on the host has to change
settings.onlyTrustTheClient: Only trust the client IP headers from the configured proxies, rejecting spoofed values from untrusted peers.
settings.optionalNameValuePairs: Optional Name: value pairs, one per line. For custom HTML, set Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8.
settings.optionalSetThisAs: Optional. Set this as the provider's back-channel logout URL and CPM will end a user's sessions when the identity provider ends theirs.
settings.plainTextJsonOr: Plain text, JSON, or custom HTML. Empty is allowed.
settings.pngIcoSvgWebp: PNG, ICO, SVG, WebP, GIF or JPEG, up to 256 KB. A square image of at least 32×32 works everywhere; browsers scale it down themselves.
settings.pointAtAHeadscale: Point at a Headscale or other coordination server. Empty uses Tailscale's own.
settings.pointYourMonitoringTool: Point your monitoring tool at the metrics endpoint
settings.prometheusCompatibleScrapeEndpoint: Prometheus-compatible scrape endpoint, exposed on a dedicated port.
settings.recordEveryProxiedRequest: Record every proxied request and every WAF event, and show them on the Analytics page. With this off, no events are written and the agents stop reading Caddy's logs.

analytics_enabled.description: Collect traffic and WAF events. With an agent running the stack, turning this on also starts the ClickHouse container — no Compose profile needed. Leave unset to decide from whether a password is configured below.
analytics_enabled.label: Enable analytics

app_name.description: Shown in the sidebar, on the login card, and as the suffix on every page title.
app_name.label: Application name

auth_allow_oauth_registration.description: Let a first-time OAuth identity create an account. Separate from self-registration: with this off, existing users can still sign in and link.
auth_allow_oauth_registration.label: Allow OAuth registration

auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.description: Let the provider's claims set a new user's role and status. With this off they are forced to user/active regardless of what the IdP sends. Only enable it for an IdP you control.
auth_allow_oauth_role_from_claims.label: Trust IdP role claims

auth_allow_self_registration.description: Let anyone create an account with an email address and password.
auth_allow_self_registration.label: Allow self-registration

auth_disable_local_users.description: Remove local accounts entirely: no credential sign-in, no password management, no bootstrap admin. Enable only once OAuth sign-in is confirmed working.
auth_disable_local_users.label: OIDC-only mode

auth_rate_limit_enabled.description: Throttle requests to the auth endpoints. Separate from the login throttle below.
auth_rate_limit_enabled.label: Rate-limit auth requests

auth_rate_limit_max.description: How many auth requests one client may make before being throttled.
auth_rate_limit_max.label: Auth requests per window

auth_rate_limit_window.description: The period over which auth requests are counted.
auth_rate_limit_window.label: Auth rate-limit window (seconds)

auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.description: Require anyone still on a pre-argon2id bcrypt hash to change their password. Leave unset to let the Security toggle decide.
auth_require_password_change_on_legacy_h.label: Force a reset for legacy password hashes

auth_trust_host.description: Build URLs from the request's Host header. Only behind a proxy that rewrites it, and only when the public URL above cannot cover the setup.
auth_trust_host.label: Trust the Host header

avatar_gravatar.description: Let user icons fall back to gravatar.com, which the browser fetches directly. Turn off to keep every avatar lookup off the network.
avatar_gravatar.label: Gravatar fallback

base_url.description: The address users reach this instance at. OAuth redirect URIs are built from it, so it must match what the provider has registered.
base_url.label: Public URL

caddy_api_url.description: Where Caddy's admin API is reachable, for a deployment running Caddy with no agent. With an agent, every admin call is proxied through it and this is not used.
caddy_api_url.label: Caddy admin API

caddy_build_timeout.description: How long to wait for an xcaddy rebuild before giving up. Caddy compiles from source, so slow or ARM hosts can take considerably longer than the default.
caddy_build_timeout.label: Caddy build timeout (seconds)

clickhouse_db.description: The database traffic and WAF events are written to.
clickhouse_db.label: ClickHouse database

clickhouse_password.description: Required for analytics: the ClickHouse container refuses to start without one, and with it empty there is nothing to authenticate as.
clickhouse_password.label: ClickHouse password

clickhouse_retention_days.description: How long traffic and WAF events are kept. Lowering it uses less disk, and migrates the existing tables' TTL on the next start.
clickhouse_retention_days.label: Analytics retention (days)

clickhouse_url.description: Where the analytics database is reachable.
clickhouse_url.label: ClickHouse URL

clickhouse_user.description: The account traffic and WAF events are written as.
clickhouse_user.label: ClickHouse user

forward_auth_internal_url.description: The address Caddy uses to reach this app for forward_auth. Derived from the container network when empty; set it only if that derivation is wrong.
forward_auth_internal_url.label: Internal forward-auth address

geoip_enabled.description: Country lookups for analytics and geo blocking. With an agent running the stack, turning this on also starts the geoipupdate container. Leave unset to decide from whether the databases are already present.
geoip_enabled.label: Enable GeoIP

geoipupdate_account_id.description: Needed to download GeoLite2 databases, which geo blocking depends on.
geoipupdate_account_id.label: MaxMind account ID

geoipupdate_license_key.description: Issued alongside the account ID at maxmind.com.
geoipupdate_license_key.label: MaxMind license key

login_block_ms.description: How long a blocked client stays blocked.
login_block_ms.label: Lockout duration (milliseconds)

login_max_attempts.description: How many failed sign-ins one client may make before it is blocked.
login_max_attempts.label: Failed logins before lockout

login_window_ms.description: The period over which failed sign-ins are counted.
login_window_ms.label: Login window (milliseconds)

update_check_enabled.description: Ask the registry below, a few times a day, whether a newer release has been published. The only request this app makes to the internet on its own; turn it off to make none.
update_check_enabled.label: Check for updates

update_image_repository.description: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name — the update check reads its tags. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, or it will report releases you cannot pull.
update_image_repository.label: Image repository

settings.requireAPasswordChange: Require a password change for users still on an older hash
settings.resolutionHappensAtConfig: Resolution happens at config save/reload time and resolved IPs are written into Caddy's active config. If one handler has multiple different HTTPS upstream hostnames, HTTPS pinning is skipped for those HTTPS upstreams to avoid SNI mismatch.
settings.resolvesUpstreamHostnamesAt: Resolves upstream hostnames at config-apply time and writes IPs into Caddy's active config.
settings.runsATailscaleNode: Runs a Tailscale node inside Caddy. A proxy host can then be served privately on your tailnet, gated on tailnet identity, or proxied to a backend that only exists on the tailnet.
settings.separateFromAdminApi: Separate from admin API on port 2019.
settings.shorthandForNamingThe: Shorthand for naming the role groups: with prefix CPM_, members of CPM_Admin become admins, CPM_User users and CPM_Viewer viewers. Name the groups below instead if they do not share a prefix.
settings.shownInTheBrowser: Shown in the browser tab and in bookmarks
settings.sixLettersFromThe: Six letters, from the agent's logs.
settings.theAgentStartsAnd: The agent starts and stops ClickHouse for you
settings.theAgentStartsAnd2: The agent starts and stops geoipupdate for you
settings.theProviderBecomesAuthoritative: The provider becomes authoritative: a user who loses the admin group is demoted on their next sign-in. The last remaining admin is never demoted.
settings.theTailnetMachineName: The tailnet machine name used by hosts that do not name one of their own. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.
settings.theTailscaleModuleIs: The Tailscale module is not enabled
settings.theseErrorPagesApply: These error pages apply to every proxy host as a fallback. A per-host error page for the same status code takes precedence.
settings.thisFixesClientIp: This fixes client-IP attribution everywhere at once — access logs, analytics, the country map, and any downstream handler using the client_ip placeholder.
settings.thisPolicyIsSet: This policy is set by the AUTH_REQUIRE_PASSWORD_CHANGE_ON_LEGACY_HASH environment variable
settings.thisProviderSCaddy: This provider's Caddy module is disabled
settings.unmatchedConnectionsAreClosed: Unmatched connections are closed without a response
settings.useGravatarWhenA: Use Gravatar when a user has no icon
settings.useTheseRangesAs: Use these ranges as the default trusted-proxy list for global geoblocking so the two can't silently disagree. A geoblock list set explicitly wins.
settings.usedByLetS: Used by Let's Encrypt for expiry notifications.
settings.usefulWhenYourDns: Useful when your DNS provider has slow propagation or when using split-horizon DNS. Common public resolvers: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare), 194.242.2.2 (Mullvad), 9.9.9.9 (Quad9).

validation.tristate: {label} must be true, false, or left unset

settings.viewWithDockerExec: View with: docker exec caddy-proxy-manager-caddy tail -f /logs/access.log
settings.whatToCallThis: What to call this agent here. Defaults to its hostname.
settings.whereEachNodeKeeps: Where each node keeps its identity, one subdirectory per node. Must be on a volume, or every restart registers a new machine.
settings.whereTheAnalyticsDatabase: Where the analytics database is reachable.
settings.whereThisDeploymentS: Where this deployment's images come from, without the image name. Point it at your own namespace if you run a fork, or it will report releases you cannot pull.

setup.aDatabaseFromA: A database from a previous version is on this host. Migrating copies the parts you choose into PostgreSQL. The original file is not modified.

account.agentDescription: An agent no longer shares this application's setup. Finish the controller first, then pair the agent to it from Settings.
account.displayNameHelp: Shown on the sign-in button, e.g. Authentik or Keycloak.
account.heading: Set up Caddy Proxy Manager
account.migratedDescription: Everything you chose from {source} is already in place. You asked to leave the old users behind, so this instance still needs its first administrator.
account.migratedTitle: Your data was migrated, but its accounts were not
account.redirectUriDescription: Your provider needs to allow this instance's /api/auth/callback/oauth2 address, or the sign-in on the next screen will fail.
account.roleHelp: The controller is the dashboard and its database. An agent manages Caddy on one host and is configured from the controller once this is finished.
account.subtitle: Nothing can sign in to this instance yet. Create the first administrator, or point it at an identity provider.

setup.addOrChangeProviders: Add or change providers from Settings once setup is finished.
setup.anythingLeftUntickedStays: Anything left unticked stays in the old file, which is not modified either way.
setup.dotSeparatedForA: Dot-separated for a nested claim, e.g. resource_access.cpm.roles.

errors.clientIdAndSecretRequired: A client ID and secret are required.
errors.issuerMustBeUrl: The issuer must be a URL starting with http:// or https://.
errors.passwordsDiffer: The two passwords do not match.
errors.providerSaveFailed: Could not save the provider. Check the values and try again.

setup.everythingIsReEncrypted: Everything is re-encrypted with the SESSION_SECRET this deployment already uses, so the old one is needed for this import and never again. Migrating without it would leave those secrets unreadable, and each would have to be entered again by hand.
setup.everythingYouChoseTo: Everything you chose to bring across is now in PostgreSQL, and the application is running from it.
setup.filledInFromYour: Filled in from your OAUTH_ environment variables
setup.fromTheEnvThat: From the .env that installation ran with, exactly as it appears there. It is checked before anything is written, used to re-encrypt these values under this deployment's own key, and not stored.
setup.keepACopyOf: Keep a copy of the old database
setup.linkToAnExisting: Link to an existing account with the same email
setup.mapRolesFromThe: Map roles from the provider's groups
setup.mirrorTheRemainingPrefixed: Mirror the remaining prefixed groups into this app's groups
setup.noAccountsWillBe: No accounts will be brought across
setup.nothingReadsThisFile: Nothing reads this file any more
setup.nothingToRemoveNone: Nothing to remove — none of the settings you migrated were configured by an environment variable.
setup.offMeansAReturning: Off means a returning user with a matching local account is refused rather than merged.
setup.offMeansEveryoneArrives: Off means everyone arrives with the default role below, whatever groups they are in.
setup.offeredFirstWhenYou: Offered first when you create a proxy host, so the one you use most belongs here.
setup.savingStoresTheProvider: Saving stores the provider in the database, after which those variables can be removed.
setup.signInThroughAn: Sign in through an OIDC provider, as well as or instead of local accounts. Leave these blank to skip — one can be added from Settings at any time.
setup.skipTheMigrationAnd: Skip the migration and configure this instance from scratch. The old file is left alone, and this offer will not appear again.
setup.spaceSeparatedGroupClaims: Space separated. Group claims usually need one more than the default.
setup.theApplicationDidNot: The application did not restart on its own
setup.theApplicationNoLonger: The application no longer opens it, so any change made there from now on is invisible to it.
setup.theOldDatabaseHas: The old database has been copied. One more step before you sign in.
setup.theProviderSOidc: The provider's OIDC issuer. Its endpoints are discovered from here.
setup.theThreeEndpointsAre: The three endpoints are only needed for a provider that does not publish OIDC discovery; leave them blank otherwise.
setup.theseAreStoredIn: These are stored in the database once you save, so they can be changed later without editing a file or restarting.
setup.theyAreFilledIn: They are filled in below and marked. Saving copies them into the database, after which you can remove those entries from your .env.
setup.thisCopiesRowsWith: This copies rows with their original identifiers, so it expects nothing to have been created here yet. Running it against a database that is already in use is not supported.
setup.thisDatabaseWasEncrypted: This database was encrypted with a different key
setup.whereLetSEncrypt: Where Let's Encrypt sends expiry warnings and account notices. Optional, and worth setting: without it nobody is told when a certificate is about to lapse.
setup.withCpmMembershipOf: With CPM_, membership of CPM_Admin grants admin. The three fields below override it.
setup.youDoNotHave: You do not have to keep the old secret
setup.yourDataIsIn: Your data is in PostgreSQL. The application is restarting so it runs from it: this process started against an empty database and is still working from what it read then.

users.manageUserAccountsRoles: Manage user accounts, roles, and access.

waf.chooseAValidCustom: Choose a valid custom time range
waf.configureTheGlobalWeb: Configure the global Web Application Firewall. Per-host settings can merge with or override these defaults. Powered by Coraza with optional OWASP Core Rule Set.
waf.coversSqliXssLfi: Covers SQLi, XSS, LFI, RCE — recommended.
waf.exclusionsAreSavedBut: Exclusions are saved but have no effect until WAF is enabled.
waf.largestRequestBodyThe: Largest request body the WAF will inspect.
waf.modsecuritySeclangSyntaxApplied: ModSecurity SecLang syntax. Applied after OWASP CRS if enabled.
waf.mustNotExceedThe: Must not exceed the request body limit.
waf.noAuditDataAvailable: No audit data available for this event.
waf.noWafEventsFound: No WAF events found. Enable the WAF in Settings and send some traffic to see events here.
waf.rejectReturns413Partial: Reject returns 413; Partial inspects what fits and forwards the rest.
waf.ruleExclusionsLiveOn: Rule exclusions live on the Suppressed Rules tab
waf.rulesListedHereAre: Rules listed here are suppressed globally via SecRuleRemoveById for all proxy hosts using global WAF settings.
waf.searchByHostIp: Search by host, IP, URI, or rule message...
waf.searchByRuleId: Search by rule ID or message…
waf.theCorazaWafModule: The Coraza WAF module is disabled
waf.webApplicationFirewallEvents: Web Application Firewall events and rule management.
